content.doc_md:
To fill a table in MySQL, use the "INSERT INTO" statement.

To insert multiple rows into a table, use theexecutemany()method.

The second parameter of theexecutemany()method 
is a list of tuples, containing the data you want to insert:

You can get the id of the row you 
just inserted by asking the cursor object.

### Code Snippets

```
import mysql.connector
mydb = mysql.connector.connect(
host="localhost",
user="
yourusername
",
password="
yourpassword
",
database="mydatabase"
)
mycursor = mydb.cursor()
sql = "INSERT INTO customers (name, 
  address) VALUES (%s, %s)"
val = ("John", "Highway 21")
mycursor.execute(sql, 
  val)
mydb.commit()
print(mycursor.rowcount, "record inserted.")
```
